finding: None of the downloaded pretrained checkpoints is accompanied by a complete identity manifest. The local verification artifacts expose no compatible real-name identity mapping (FG-NET exposes benchmark-local numeric IDs only). Therefore identity-level pretraining/benchmark intersection cannot be computed and must not be reported as zero.
risk: Overlap cannot be excluded, especially for web-scale or celebrity-oriented pretraining sets and celebrity benchmarks. This limits claims of benchmark independence.
mitigations: Report each checkpoint, checksum and declared pretraining dataset.
Keep every benchmark evaluation-only and never tune thresholds on benchmark identities.
Report results across CASIA- and WebFace-pretrained model families rather than relying on one lineage.
State the unresolved overlap risk in the model card and limitations.
Re-run the exact intersection if upstream identity manifests and compatible benchmark mappings become available.
